# program text 1
program Meeting recap in the Note
  goal
  > After a meeting, the meeting's Note should end with a short recap: the decisions, the actions with their owners, and the open questions. It comes from the transcript we already keep, runs on the local model, and sends nothing out. It is a section of the Note that I can edit, not a new window.
  >
  > It must be fast: under 20 seconds after Stop on this Mac. It must not make up owners: when nobody was named, it says "No owner". Alice asked for this for her team's standups, so she sees it before it ships.
  in app · main · project HoldSpeak
  template build and review
  control normal
  check scripts/quick_check.sh
  budget 64k

every step
  R1 review: The change does only what its brief says.
  R2 review: Each new behaviour has a test.

at the end
  R+ measure: The recap appears in the Note within 20 seconds of Stop on the owner's Mac.
    run scripts/quick_check.sh
    bound total < 20 s
  R+ word: Alice has seen the recap section in her team's standup Note before this ships.

step + Generate recap from transcript via local model
  owns holdspeak/services/note_outcomes_service.py, holdspeak/memory/local_model.py
  brief
  > Add a generate_recap function to the note outcomes service. It takes the meeting's stored transcript, calls the local model (no network egress), and returns a structured recap: a list of decisions, a list of actions each with an owner name, and a list of open questions. The output is plain text formatted as a "Recap" section ready to append to the Note.
  R+ check: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_desk_note_outcomes.py -x` is green.

step + Enforce "No owner" when no name is in the transcript
  owns holdspeak/plugins/builtin/action_owner_enforcer.py, holdspeak/runtime/ownership.py
  after 1
  brief
  > In the recap's action list, if the transcript does not name a person for an action, the owner field is the literal string "No owner". The enforcer plugin never infers, guesses, or fabricates an owner from surrounding context.
  R+ check: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_action_owner_enforcer_plugin.py -x` is green.

step + Wire recap into meeting Stop and append to the Note
  owns holdspeak/runtime/meeting_stop.py, holdspeak/meeting_session/models.py
  after 1, 2
  brief
  > On meeting Stop, call generate_recap with the transcript, then append the result as a "Recap" section to the meeting's Note record. The section is part of the Note's editable text, not a separate window or pullout.
  R+ check: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_meeting_stop_and_conflicts.py -x` is green.

step + Render and edit the Recap section in the Note editor
  owns web/src/desk/pullouts/editors/NoteEditor.tsx, web/src/desk/noteOutcomes.ts
  after 3
  brief
  > The Note editor renders the "Recap" section as an editable block at the end of the Note. The owner can add, remove, or reword lines. No new window, pullout, or route is introduced.
  R+ shot: The Note window at 1440 shows the Recap section as editable text at the bottom of the Note, with no clipped text.

# program text 1
program Meeting recap in the Note                 # Drafting · 0 of 4 done
  goal
  > After a meeting, the meeting's Note should end with a short recap: the decisions, the actions with their owners, and the open questions. It comes from the transcript we already keep, runs on the local model, and sends nothing out. It is a section of the Note that I can edit, not a new window.
  >
  > It must be fast: under 20 seconds after Stop on this Mac. It must not make up owners: when nobody was named, it says "No owner". Alice asked for this for her team's standups, so she sees it before it ships.
